summary: The GPO Modernization Act of 2026 updates the programs, operations, and oversight of the Government Publishing Office (GPO). It modernizes the Federal Depository Library Program to include digital formats, establishes a National Collection of U.S. Government Public Information, updates internal GPO administrative and procurement authorities, renames the Joint Committee on Printing to the Joint Committee on Publishing, and replaces hardbound publication requirements for the Library of Congress's Constitution Annotated with digital versions.

affected_groups.effect: Gains updated operational authorities, gift acceptance capabilities, a higher simplified acquisition threshold, adjusted employee leave carryover rules, and revised oversight under the renamed Joint Committee on Publishing.

Allowed to use digital information substitutes, designate digital-only libraries, and dispose of certain unwanted government publications under new Superintendent of Documents guidelines, while no longer being required to maintain a minimum number of physical books.
Shifted from producing hardbound editions and supplements of the Constitution Annotated to preparing and publishing them exclusively in digital formats online.
Gains guaranteed free permanent public access to digital government information through an online system with protected user privacy.

key_provisions: Updates the Federal Depository Library Program to encompass government public information in all formats, including digital, and removes minimum book maintenance requirements for depository libraries.
Establishes the National Collection of U.S. Government Public Information and requires the GPO to operate a digital repository system that protects user privacy.
Redesignates the Joint Committee on Printing as the Joint Committee on Publishing and updates its structure and oversight responsibilities.
Raises the simplified acquisition threshold for GPO purchases from $100,000 to $350,000 and authorizes the GPO to accept gifts and bequests of property.

Replaces the requirement for the Library of Congress to produce hardbound editions and supplements of the Constitution Annotated with digital online versions beginning after the October 2026 Supreme Court term.

It modernizes the Federal Depository Library Program to include digital formats, establishes a National Collection of U.S. Government Public Information, updates internal GPO administrative and procurement authorities, renames the Joint Committee on Printing to the Joint Committee on Publishing, and replaces hardbound publication requirements for the Library of Congress's Constitution Annotated with digital versions.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a moderate modernization of federal publishing and public information laws, transitioning traditional print-heavy mandates and library requirements into digital-first formats while adjusting internal GPO administrative authorities.
